item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Pica Code IR-2026-109 Development of Advanced Life Cycle Assessment and Life Cycle Costing Models and Tools for the Environmental Characterization of Products, Processes, Services or Organizations (Univ. MODENA e R. E.)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-24 13:00
Institution: Univ. MODENA e R. E., Reggio Emilia
Field: Chemistry / 03/CHEM-06 Fondamenti chimici delle tecnologie

The research activity will focus on the development of integrated Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and Life Cycle Costing (LCC) models and tools to support decision-making for products, processes, services or organizations. It will address the definition and integration of environmental and economic variables, parameters, indicators, and life cycle inventories. Models will be developed for hotspot identification, trade-off assessment, and comparison of alternative life cycle scenarios, including sensitivity and uncertainty analyses. The resulting tools will support improvement strategies, management decisions, and environmental and economic performance assessment and reporting.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Development of solid/quasi-solid (bio)-polymer electrolytes for sustainable rechargeable batteries - Ref.114/26/IR (Politecnico TORINO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-12 15:00
Institution: Politecnico TORINO, Torino
Field: Chemistry / 03/CHEM-06 Fondamenti chimici delle tecnologie

Within the European HIPERZAB project (GA 101115421), the research aims to develop biopolymer-based gel electrolytes for electrically rechargeable zinc-air batteries intended for stationary renewable energy storage over days or weeks. The focus will be on mildly acidic formulations and their integration into bilayer architectures with alkaline electrolytes. The objective is to correlate material composition, structure and properties to improve ionic conductivity, interfacial stability, water retention and operational lifetime. item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Engineering of Catalytic Active Sites on Nanocarbons for Enhancement of Photocatalysis (Univ. PADOVA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-16 13:00
Institution: Univ. PADOVA, Padova
Field: Chemistry / 03/CHEM-03 Chimica generale e inorganica

The research programme aims to develop catalytic systems based on non-noble metals for the selective semi-hydrogenation of acetylene to ethylene under visible light, using water as a proton source. Activities will focus on the design, synthesis and characterization of first-row transition-metal complexes and the evaluation of their activity in combination with photosensitizers. Relationships between complex structure, electrochemical properties and catalytic performance will be investigated to optimize efficiency,selectivity and stability. item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-26 14:00
Institution: Univ. BRESCIA, Brescia
Field: Chemistry / 03/CHEM-06 Fondamenti chimici delle tecnologie

The research activity will focus on the development, synthesis, and characterization of advanced materials for CO₂ capture and conversion. The work will involve the design and preparation of innovative materials, including adsorbents, catalysts, and multifunctional materials, with tailored physicochemical properties for the selective interaction with CO₂ and its subsequent conversion into higher-value products. item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Analysis of SMC waste for qualification for recycling processes (Univ. BOLOGNA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-15 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Chemistry / 03/CHEM-04 Chimica industriale

The ultimate objective of the REACT-FIBER project is to develop, validate and demonstrate at pilot scale an integrated, industrially scalable technological supply chain for the high-value recycling of Carbon Fiber Sheet Molding Compound (CF-SMC) materials. The activities planned under this assignment relate to OR2: Analysis of the quality of carbon fibers recycled from SMC, with particular reference to: • A2.1 – Optimization of carbon fiber recycling from cured SMC • A2.2 – Assessment of the feasibility of extending the recycling process to uncured scrap

item.description:

Field: Chemistry / 03/CHEM-01 Chimica analitica, ambientale e dei beni culturali

The research activity will focus on the development and characterization of biomimetic and edible nanozymes with catalytic activity toward glucose oxidation, to be integrated into electrochemical platforms for its ultrasensitive and selective determination.
